summary: Windows workstations unable to establish corporate VPN after security kernel patch enforces driver signature policy
description:
Issue summary:
After the Windows security rollup KB released on 2026-03-09 (applied via our patch baseline), a subset of corporate Windows 11 laptops fail to establish the corporate VPN. The VPN client reports a driver load failure.

Impact:
- ~18 employees reported inability to reach private services (internal dashboards, build agents).
- Affected users are primarily on corporate-managed laptops running the company image in us-west and us-east regions.

Observed behavior:
- VPN client (CorpVPN v3.7.2) fails with error: 'KMCI driver failed to load: STATUS_INVALID_IMAGE_HASH' or 'driver signature enforcement blocked'.
- Event Viewer Security/System logs show CodeIntegrity (CI) or KMCI errors referencing driver signature validation.
- Attempts to reinstall the VPN package do not clear the error unless a signed driver build is used.

Expected behavior:
- Workstations should continue to authenticate and establish VPN post-update without manual intervention.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start from corporate image (Win11 22H2 with our standard image + KB-2026-03-09 applied).
2) Install CorpVPN v3.7.2 (standard SCCM package) and reboot.
3) Attempt to connect to VPN. Observe client error and driver load failure in Event Viewer.

Initial hypothesis:
- The security patch hardened kernel module signature checks (KMCI) and our distributed VPN driver binary is signed with a legacy SHA1-based timestamp/signature that no longer satisfies the new enforcement.
- SCCM deploys unsigned/internally-signed test variants to some pilot pools which now fail when CI validates signatures strictly.

Relevant logs and artifacts:
- Sample EventLog excerpt (redacted) attached in ticket comments.
- Device-local CodeIntegrity error: '0xC0000425 - STATUS_INVALID_IMAGE_HASH' repeated on boot.
- SCCM deployment report shows 14 devices in failed state for latest CorpVPN push.

Business impact and priority rationale:
- Internal engineering productivity reduction; can block CI agents and remote dev work. Marking P1/Sev1 to prioritize cross-team response (Endpoint, Security, and SRE).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Lorenzo Kim (Endpoint): Confirmed two reproductions on Dell units in lab. Attached event log snippets. Opening kernel-mode signing investigation with Security.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Priya Nair (Security): Initial analysis shows corp VPN driver signed with SHA1+RSA timestamp from 2020. CI policy in KB forces SHA256/timestamp validation. Contacted VPN vendor for re-signed binaries and requested CI-compliant package ASAP.

2026-03-10 14:30 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Workaround validated: enabling a temporary GPO 'Turn off automatic root certificates updates' is NOT recommended. Instead, for testing only we used 'bcdedit /set nointegritychecks ON' on one lab device to demonstrate signature bypass — NOT for production. Documented in confluence link below.
2026-03-11 08:44 - QA (Automations): Confirmed alternate client (CorpVPN-lite v3.6.9-signed) works on affected units. Filing follow-up to validate feature parity.

2026-03-12 16:50 - Sophie Martinez (Reporter): Several remote engineers reported workaround of connecting from personal hotspots (bypassing corp network) allowed partial access to ticketing but not private build agents.

2026-03-13 10:05 - Ravi Patel (Assignee): Uploaded signed driver package from vendor (signed with SHA256) to SCCM test collection. Rolling to 50 pilot devices now. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/endpoint-tools/pull/342
investigation_notes: Reproduced on Dell Latitude 7440 and Lenovo X1 labs using corp image with latest update applied.
Confirmed CodeIntegrity strict mode enabled after KB: registry HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\CI\Policy shows enforcement level 3.

SCCM reported mixed driver versions: older legacy driver (v1.14, signed SHA1) and newer test driver (v1.15 unsigned) present in different collections — likely root cause for inconsistent user reports.
Vendor-supplied signed driver (v1.16) passes local 'signtool verify /pa' and loads successfully on test devices.
No evidence of malicious tampering; signature format is the incompatibility.
Cross-checked with Windows KB advisory: 'Enforcement for driver signature timestamp and hashing' — matches our lab behaviors.
SRE validated that CI enforcement does not affect cloud-hosted build agents (not relevant), impact limited to endpoint worker nodes behind VPN.
resolution_notes: Short-term workaround: Deploy vendor-signed driver v1.16 via SCCM to affected collections. Pilot rollout to 50 devices completed 2026-03-13 09:00 PST — all pilot devices successfully connected to VPN.
Rollback mitigation: Avoid using 'bcdedit /set nointegritychecks ON' in production; documented as unsafe in Confluence.

Long-term fix: Update packaging pipeline to require SHA256-signed drivers and add a preflight CI step to validate signature algorithm and timestamp. Created follow-up task INT-20905 to track packaging changes.
Deployment notes: Full rollout scheduled 2026-03-14 02:00-04:00 UTC to avoid peak hours; SCCM servicing window created and communicated to desktop mailing list.
Communication: Notified impacted internal channels #endpoint-support and #incidents; drafted customer-facing note for any external partners if needed.

Postmortem owner: Priya Nair (Security) to lead postmortem and update security baseline endpoint hardening doc. Postmortem link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENDPOINT/VPN+driver+signing+postmortem
